Provenance levels: provisional (placeholder, no better basis), concept (estimated from the concept renders modular1/2/3.png, scale fixed by COTS parts; see DESIGN_PLAN.md sec. 2 for the method and +-uncertainty), datasheet (COTS manufacturer data, URL given), cad / measured (none yet). Images give proportions, not dimensions: every concept value carries the uncertainty stated in its 'estimate'.

body_size_lwh.source: modular1.png (scout concept), modular2.png (lifter concept), modular3.png (cargo concept)
body_size_lwh.estimate: ITERATION 5. L x W (mating planes) x H. The image's own COTS rulers (D435 90 mm on the scout front edge, Arducam 38 mm on the cargo/lifter front) give W 0.16-0.18 m (overlay: cad_v1/images/width_overlay.jpg), but the same rulers make the side face only 0.24-0.30 m long, which cannot hold a reciprocal dock between two 97 mm wheels, and leave 79 mm between the wheels (micro motors only). W = 0.26 is set by the drivetrain: two Pololu 25D gearmotors (67 mm + coupling each) facing each other need ~160 mm between the wheel inner faces; it also restores the concept's near-square, squat footprint (L/W 1.32 vs concept 1.1-1.4). Consequence: COTS parts look ~1/3 smaller relative to the body than drawn. L from the dock-between-wheels constraint (>= 0.34 m); H from the dock/wheel rulers (78-90 mm). Uncertainty: L +-15 %; W is an engineering choice (image says 0.17).

docking.states_mapping_v1: Per connection: HOOK_A = the hook of the rover whose face is listed first in the coupling (initiator), HOOK_B = the partner's hook. Each face carries one hook (manifest name hook_<face>_a) and one pin (<face>_pin).
docking.partner_acquisition_proposal: No face tags (the dock fills the face). Top tags lie flat at 0.107-0.150 m and are seen almost edge-on (<5 deg) by the forward cameras (0.10-0.16 m high) at docking range, so they are only usable from the optional overhead camera. Proposal: (1) far field: overhead camera / fleet map gives the partner pose to +-5 cm; (2) mid field (1.0-0.3 m): a 30 mm tag36h11 on a 45 deg facet of the top bevel above each dock face (bevel grown locally from 9 to ~25 mm; top contact pad moves 10 mm down) is visible to a forward camera at 45 deg off-normal; (3) near field (<0.3 m): odometry + magnet pull-in (+-9 mm capture) + hook-sensed engagement, as TagDockingController already does. Alternative for (2): print the tag on the C-bracket faces (bracket must widen from 7 to ~30 mm, changing the concept look).

partner_acquisition.note: far: overhead camera / fleet map; mid (0.3-1.5 m): 30 mm tag on the 45 deg bevel facet above each dock face, seen by the approaching rover's front camera; close (<0.3 m): odometry + magnet capture (+-9 mm) + hook sensing. The lifter's camera faces forward but it docks rear/sides: it acquires front-on, turns, and closes on odometry.
